centre_guide.text: Welcome to the Causeway! Most of the columns have six sides. Some have four, five, seven, even eight. There are no sides on the sea. We've checked.
The tallest columns are about 12 metres high. They're basalt, so they won't be moved. Visitors, on the other hand, move quite a lot.

geologist.text: Sixty million years ago this was lava. Now it's a staircase. If that doesn't make you feel small, I'll draw you a diagram.
The columns formed as the lava cooled and shrank. It cracked in a regular pattern, like drying mud. The hexagon wins because it uses the least crack for the most room.

visitor.text: I wished on the Wishing Chair. I wished for a cup of tea. I got a coach party, but the tea followed.
Everyone talks about Fionn. Nobody asks about his wife, who was the cleverest person in the legend. She baked a griddle into a loaf and fed it to the rival.

local_man.text: I've lived beside the Causeway sixty years. The rocks haven't changed. I have.
They say a pony the colour of sea foam gallops the waves off here in the mist. Manannan's horse, the old ones called it. Mind you, the old ones also said the tide could be bribed.
